claims: The BA.3.2 strain is nicknamed "Cicada".
The "Cicada" variant (BA.3.2) is a highly mutated Omicron subvariant.
The "Cicada" variant (BA.3.2) has been detected in dozens of states.
The "Cicada" variant (BA.3.2) has many mutations.
"Stratus" and "Nimbus" are circulating variants identified in early 2026.
The "Stratus" variant often causes hoarseness and raspy voices.
2026 COVID-19 variants are frequently characterized by severe, sharp throat pain.
2026 COVID-19 variants are frequently characterized by intense congestion.
2026 COVID-19 is characterized by "Razorblade" throat, a severe, sharp, or intense sore throat.
2026 COVID-19 causes congestion and running nose with heavy sinus pressure.
2026 COVID-19 causes persistent dry cough that often produces no mucus.
Fever or chills are often present in early stages of 2026 COVID-19.
2026 COVID-19 causes fatigue and weakness with significant exhaustion.
2026 COVID-19 causes headache.
2026 COVID-19 causes muscle or body aches.
Loss of taste or smell is less common in 2026 COVID-19 than in early pandemic years.
COVID-19 symptoms often appear 2–14 days after exposure.
2026 COVID-19 symptoms are very similar to influenza (flu) and RSV.
2026 COVID-19 symptoms, influenza, and RSV are often indistinguishable.
Most at-home rapid tests are still effective at detecting newer 2026 COVID-19 variants
